findings.claim: The gate-bound frozen-schema-array regression does not completely encode the newly normative equivalence requirement. The Spec explicitly requires raw-array versus frozen-tuple equivalence for required, combinators, prefixItems and dependentRequired, covering both validation and charging, but the committed test contains no dependentRequired schema and only checks selected violations/event-ID presence rather than exact raw-versus-frozen trace equality.
findings.evidence: The production implementation currently handles tuples correctly, and an independent active counterexample confirmed identical rules and full traces for all four keyword families. However, test_frozen_schema_arrays_preserve_required_combinator_and_prefix_semantics only constructs required, anyOf and prefixItems; it never constructs dependentRequired. It compares neither raw and frozen validation outputs nor their complete charge traces. GEW-ADR3-SCHEMA-FROZEN-R binds this incomplete test, while the independent production-trace oracle exercises frozen anyOf but no dependentRequired or prefixItems schema. A future list-only regression in dependentRequired—or an ordering/count regression while schema.branch/schema.item remain present—would therefore pass the frozen-array gate.
findings.required_change: Extend the gate-bound committed regression to include dependentRequired and assert raw JSON-list versus registry-frozen tuple equivalence for validation failures and complete canonical charge traces across required, combinators, prefixItems and dependentRequired. Keep the exact test binding and add an independent-oracle vector where needed so each affected frozen-array behavior is mechanically regression-protected.
